programme.title: Ancient Powers
programme.desc: The creators of the six-episode series, using advanced computer graphics, will present the history of the five most powerful civilizations of antiquity: Egypt, China, India, Rome and Greece.Ancient powers have a lot in common.In the fight for survival and domination, they went through similar stages of development.They conquered new territories, built societies and political systems, as well as formed cultures, developed trade, ideas and the art of war.Viewers will learn about the latest archaeological research on ancient powers.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2
programme.desc: More than seven years have passed since the premiere of the second season of the nature super-production, but it still impresses with its great implementation.Its creators completed 125 expeditions in 39 countries over four years.They spent over six thousand hours diving in the depths and filming the coasts.The best scenes were selected from this spectacular material, taking viewers to inaccessible worlds.Their guide is Sir David Attenborough, who claims that we know less about the depths of our own planet than about the surface of Mars.The inhabitants of the ocean's depths influence our lives because they shape the climate and produce about half of the oxygen necessary for the functioning of the planet.They are also home to numerous representatives of the fauna kingdom.The development of technology has allowed man to look into their world, which was previously inaccessible.Scientists are also constantly expanding their knowledge of animal behavior.The first episode of the program is a journey through the waters surrounding the Seychelles, New Zealand, Japan and the Arctic.Filmmakers captured, among others, dolphins surfing in the Red Sea.They tracked walruses resting on melting ice in the Arctic.They followed killer whales and humpback whales feasting on herring schools in Norway.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2
programme.desc: For centuries, humanity has believed that the oceans are so vast and their inhabitants are so numerous that human activity cannot harm them.It is now known that this is not true.The existence of many animal species associated with the ocean ecosystem is at risk.This is clearly visible in the example of herring.Overfishing wiped out their population 50 years ago.Currently, thanks to good management, it has been reborn.Human-made noise, industrial pollution and plastic waste also negatively impact ocean life.In turn, more than 2/3 of the world's coral reefs have suffered from global warming.Recent research has revealed that the chemical composition of ocean waters is changing.They become acidic due to carbon dioxide dissolving in them.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2
programme.desc: In Southeast Asia there is the so-calledThe Coral Triangle, an area containing the richest reef in the world.In this vibrant place, there is constant competition for space, food and a mate.Coral reefs, which cover less than 1/10 percent of the ocean floor, support 1/4 of known marine species.Corals create complex and diverse structures.Each reef also has a clearly marked boundary beyond which lies the ocean depth.It is a kind of wall that protects the city from waves.The reefs are inhabited by, among others:cuttlefish that prey on crabs.Although this crustacean's pincers pose a great threat, cuttlefish have an extraordinary weapon - their skin contains millions of pigment cells that create constantly changing patterns.Creatures that have adapted well to life in reefs that resemble underwater cities reap many benefits.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2: The Making of
programme.desc: Behind the scenes of the creation of a spectacular nature series that took 4 years to film.The teams implementing it visited all oceans.Thanks to the fact that the divers had the latest equipment, they could have very close encounters with the animals being filmed.Even in low light conditions, the cameras captured events invisible to the human eye.Inspection cameras show the lives of small creatures, and those equipped with a suction cup record what is happening in the ocean from the perspective of larger animals.Wanting to film the most extraordinary wildlife scenes, the team also visited coastlines in the farthest corners of the world, such as the Galapagos Islands.Marine life around these islands depends on cold currents feeding surface waters.

programme.title: Where the Wild Men Are with Ben Fogle
programme.desc: Famous adventurer Ben Fogle interviews and meets people who have made a risky decision, leaving their life in Western society and settling in the middle of nowhere, far from civilization.
